# Disagreement Log — T12_005 (Testament of Issachar)
**Chapter:** T12_005 | **Verses:** 7 sections (~8 verses)
**Translators compared:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Arbiter:** SOPHIA

| # | Verse | Issue | EMET | LOGOS | PNEUMA | SOPHIA ruling |
|---|-------|-------|------|-------|--------|---------------|
| 1 | 1:6 | Mandrake description | Not described | "sweet-smelling apples...produced in the land of Haran" | "mandrakes" only | Brief description omitted — appears to be LOGOS expansion not in base MS; SOPHIA retains plain "mandrakes" |
| 2 | 2:1–3 | Angel apparition detail | Single angel to Leah | LOGOS expands: angel hearkens to Rachel, details Joseph/Benjamin | Brief mention only | SOPHIA follows EMET/PNEUMA brevity; LOGOS expansion is interpretive gloss |
| 3 | 3:1 | "simplicity" key term | "simple-man" (hyphenated) | "simplicity" and "rectitude" | "simple man" | "simplicity" — haplotēs is the chapter's defining virtue; should be foregrounded consistently |
| 4 | 6:1 | Age at death | "hundred-and-twenty-six-years-old" | No age given at this point | "126 years old" | "hundred and twenty-six years old" — preserved with EMET detail, without hyphenation |
| 5 | 7:2 | Death description | "fell-asleep-in-peace" | "fell asleep in peace" | "fell asleep in peace" | "fell asleep in peace" — all agree; consensus phrasing used throughout Testaments |

---
*SOPHIA notes: Testament of Issachar is the shortest and most positive of the Twelve — a portrait of uncorrupted virtue. The mandrakes narrative is brief but essential for establishing Issachar's birth context. The chapter's key word haplotēs (simplicity/singleness) should appear prominently and consistently.*
